title: Grothendieck structure and exact inflation for sheaf-group module actions
statement:
Fix compatible universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(C,J)$ be a small site with finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative unital rings on $C$, all with values in the coefficient universe. For a sheaf of groups $K$ on $C$ with values in that universe, define $\mathcal E_K(R)$ to consist of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] together with operations $K(U)\times M(U)\to M(U)$, natural in $U$, satisfying the unit and associativity laws and $R(U)$-linearity in $M(U)$. Its morphisms are restriction-natural linear maps commuting with these operations, with addition defined sectionwise. Give the coefficient ring the trivial action.

The category $\mathcal E_K(R)$ is Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] with this specified additive structure. The forgetful functor $U_K:\mathcal E_K(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ creates kernels and cokernels and detects exactness: kernels are sectionwise kernels, and cokernels have underlying sheaf the module sheafification of sectionwise cokernels [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], each with its induced $K$-action. In particular $U_K$ is exact and detects zero objects.

For any sheaf of groups $L$ in the same universe and any morphism of group sheaves $\theta:L\to K$, precomposition of actions defines an additive exact functor $\operatorname{Inf}_\theta:\mathcal E_K(R)\to\mathcal E_L(R)$, leaving the underlying modules and maps unchanged and setting $l\cdot_\theta m=\theta(l)\cdot m$ on every object. It preserves the displayed kernels and cokernels. These assertions include $K=1$, $L=1$, and the zero ring sheaf.

proof.text: Forgetting the action is additive by reflexivity on underlying morphisms, and faithful by extensionality of full-subcategory and subgroup morphisms. An object is zero if and only if its identity is zero; additivity and faithfulness therefore give detection of zero. The presentation creates each kernel and cokernel, so it preserves them. Mathlib Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesKernels and its colimit dual then give preservation of finite limits and finite colimits. Apply lem-per-exact-family-detection to the singleton family to obtain the exactness equivalence for short complexes.

proof.text: Evaluation of module sheaves preserves finite limits, giving the sectionwise kernel assertion. For a module-sheaf morphism f, let F be ordinary module sheafification and e the isomorphism given by the counit of its adjunction. Naturality of e identifies F applied to the underlying presheaf morphism with f, up to the isomorphisms on source and target. Mathlib cokernel.mapIso gives the corresponding isomorphism of cokernels. Compose its inverse with the inverse of PreservesCokernel.iso for F. This identifies cokernel f with sheafification of its presheaf cokernel.

proof.text: Restrict an action by composing its monoid homomorphism with theta. For the naturality equation apply the old action naturality and evaluate theta.naturality on the group section. Inflation leaves every linear map unchanged, so its additivity is reflexivity.

proof.text: Let U and V forget K and L actions, and let F be inflation. The equality F composed with V equals U is definitional on objects and maps. Singleton exact-family detection for V gives reflection of isomorphisms. Since V preserves finite limits and colimits between the abelian categories already constructed, it reflects both by Mathlib reflectsFiniteLimits_of_reflectsIsomorphisms and its dual. The finite limit and colimit preservation of U therefore implies that of F, using preservesFiniteLimits_of_reflects_of_preserves and its dual. Finally a short complex T is exact after inflation because its image under V is definitionally its original image under U, and the two forgetful functors detect exactness. No nontriviality or nonzero-ring hypothesis occurs.
